This is not only one of the very best RPGs I have played in years, but it also has great multiplayer integration! You can play with friends with shared experience and have a lot of fun exploring a world that is absolutely packed full of content! The game has several modes, but I have only gone through the regular quest so far. 

The enemies are brilliantly designed, and they each have a unique fighting style that I think added a lot to the overall experience. The combat is so enjoyable that I found myself seeking out battles wherever I could find them!

It has a LOT in common with old PC immersive sims like Thief, giving the game a very nostalgic feel. 

It is not grindy whatsoever. Enemy levels do suggest a sequence of events, but in no way are you ever blocked off with a hard wall you cannot cross. It's always possible to sneak into high-leveled areas and grab some cool loot. 

If you are someone who dislikes the path that games have been going down in recent years and wish that you could go back to when games were less grindy and restrictive, and allowed you to freely explore and enjoy the world at your own pace, then be sure to give this one a try! If you like this sort of game, you will sink in 6 hours at the absolute minimum if you do not try any other modes and you complete it quickly.

The way this game deals with resources is also brilliant. It reminds me a lot of Resident Evil, in the sense that I only ever had exactly how much was needed to make it through each given area. You can return to old areas and find useful items if necessary, but returning to old locations is not required.

NOTE: This game does not have a dialogue system or detailed quest lines. It's more about combat and battling your way through areas and dungeons.

Counter Spell ist eine interessante und kurzweilige Mischung aus Egoshooter (FPS) und Rollenspiel (RPG) und ein Geheimtipp für Fans von Indie-Spielen.

Vom Spielgefühl spielt sich das Spiel wie ein FPS, wird jedoch um diverse klassische Elemente eines RPG ergänzt. Es gibt verschiedene Klassen mit unterschiedlichen Fähigkeiten, Levelaufstiege, Skillpunkte und man sammelt immer bessere Ausrüstung, die den Charakter noch stärker macht. Vergleichbar ist das Spiel grob mit Hexen 2 und dem etwas neueren Dark Messiah of Might and Magic.

Counter Spell verfügt über diverse Spielmodi. Der Questmodus ist die typische Singleplayerkampagne, bei der man die ganze Welt nach und nach erkundet. Das Spiel ist Open World, sprich man ist lediglich durch die Gegnerstärke in seinem Vorgehen limitiert. Die Story hierbei ist eher rudimentär, jedoch kann man mehrere Bücher in der Welt finden, die die Hintergrundgeschichte recht amüsant etwas vertiefen und ausführen. Man kann die Kampagne auch Coop mit Freunden spielen. Sie dient jedoch hauptsächlich dazu, mit der Welt, den Gegner und Fähigkeiten seines Charakters vertraut zu werden und dauert etwa 5 Stunden.

Anschließend kann man entweder dort weiter bessere Items für seinen Charakter farmen, einen höheren Schwierigkeitsgrad versuchen (es gibt 3), die anderen Klassen ausprobieren oder sich in einem der anderen 9 Spielmodi mit Freunden austoben. Diese sind wahlweise auf einen Sektor der Welt begrenzt oder nutzen die gesamte Weltkarte. Man hat die Wahl zwischen klassischen PVP-Modi wie Deathmatch, Team-Deathmatch, Capture the Flag, Kingslayer, die auch teilweise interessante Abweichungen und Variationen zu den bekannten Modi bieten oder mehreren Coop-Modi mit Freunden wie das klassische Survival. In den PvP-Modi können Itemvorteile auf Wunsch deaktiviert werden, um faire Matches zu garantieren. In den Coop-Modi kann man dagegen auch bessere Ausrüstung für seinen Charakter finden.

Das Spiel liefert auch einen umfangreichen Baumodus, bei dem man wie in Minecraft eigene Karten bauen kann. Wer sich gerne kreativ austobt, kann hier mehrere Stunden verbringen.

Besonders hervorzuheben ist die herausragende Pflege des Spiels durch den Entwickler. Es gibt regelmäßige Patches mit neuen Inhalten und Bugfixes und auf Fragen oder Vorschläge im Forum wird innerhalb weniger Stunden reagiert. Das Spiel wird also ständig weiterentwickelt und verbessert, wodurch man alle paar Monate wieder reingucken kann und interessante Neuerungen findet.

Solospielzeit: 5-20 Stunden
Multiplayerspielzeit: 1-20 Stunden

+ Abwechslungsreiche Klassen
+ Unverbrauchtes und neues Spielgefühl
+ Sehr aktiver Entwickler, häufige Updates und sehr schnelle Antworten und Reaktionen im Forum
+ Viele spaßige Spielmodi

+/- Der Grafikstil ist sicherlich Geschmackssache, jedoch in sich sehr schön und absolut stimmig

- Wenig aktive Spieler, wer Multiplayermodi spielen möchte, sollte ein paar Freunde mitbringen. Es gibt zwar regelmäßíge Multiplayertreffen im Forum organisiert, jedoch aus den USA, sodass sie in Deutschland nur Nachts zwischen 2-4 Uhr stattfinden
- Rudimentäre Story, wer auf eine gute Story Wert legt, wird eher enttäuscht


Fazit: Wer Indie-Spiele sowie den Grafikstil mag und gerne etwas neues ausprobiert, sollte sich Counter Spell unbedingt anschauen.

It's an FPSRPG!
It's a MOBA!
It's an arena FPS!
It's a co-op FPS!
It's a stealth game!
No... it's all of them. It's Counter Spell!

Value: 10/10
Counter Spell gives you a sizeable amount of content for an indie game in its price range, 6 character classes (with more likely coming), and perhaps 10 (and counting) game modes. Plenty of replayability. Plus there's a map builder.

Game design/Balance: 8+/10
The 8+/10 means that the game currently gets an 8/10 but I expect it to improve over time. Currently, there are a lot of balance and game design issues, but the developer is almost constantly looking for feedback and advice. It's already better than the vast majority of indie games (and the game design beats most premium/"AAA" games IMO.
Skills and character abilities are somewhat split between PvE and PvP. (I suggested this because I've seen way too many games get their PvE content ruined with PvP-focused nerfs) There are a wide variety of abilities and items to find and use.

Developer attention: 10/10
As if Counter Spell wasn't already a bargain, the developer pays a LOT of attention to the discussion forums and feedback. Several of my suggestions have already gone into the game. The devs update the game at least once every 2 days when they aren't on vacation and I'm not seeing any sign that the updates are going to slow down. There are plenty of upcoming features and updates planned.

Graphics: 6/10
IMO the graphics are good enough. They aren't going to win awards, but most indie games have inferior graphics anyway - an indie game getting a 6/10 in graphics is like a premium game getting an 8.5/10. Besides, if you demand the absolute best graphics, then indie games aren't for you anyway.

Audio: 5/10
The in-game music is bland and forgettable. However I would suggest keeping the sound on because it gives plenty of cues about whatever's going on nearby.

Technical Quality: 10/10
This game hardly crashes and when it does, the devs fix it quickly. 3 weeks ago there was a bad patch that was causing crashes and it was fixed the next day. 

Other stuff:
-Counter Spell is quite family-friendly, unlike most similar games. There's NO gore, bad language, or otherwise questionable content. I would recommend an ESRB "Everyone 10+" rating for it.
-Additional modding support might happen in the future.

Summary:
This game is a gem. If you like any of the above-mentioned genres and it isn't in your library, shame on you. It's only 7 dollars... well worth even the full price.

If you enjoyed old RPGs like Hexen, Daggerfall, Enclave, Gauntlet or Thief, buy Counter Spell! This game may be Early Access, but you're getting a quality game with tons of content for under $10.

▼ THE GOOD ▼
● Singleplayer took me 5-6 hours with the Warlock Class the first time. About 2 hours as the Shaman the next. It takes long enough that you'll feel satisfied but short enough you won't get bored. Also you can play Singleplayer with friends :)
● The game world is a LOT bigger than you'd think! It's not Skyrim big, but big for an indie game and filled with hidden passages, loot and monsters.
● Each class has their own unique spells but most of the funnest ones are at max level so it gives you something to work towards (like the "vine-ladder" spell in the trailer). The game also let's you blatantly see what spells you'll unlock when picking a class.
● Very well balanced! You should reach level 20 (max) by the time you reach the final boss without any grinding outside of killing everything you see once. The game does a good job being tough, but not impossible and has harder modes for those who find it too easy.
● Treasure and enemies respawn so you don't need to worry if you miss anything, chances are you can find it again.
● Aside from the passive quests (kill enough enemies in zone-1, collect 3 unique items from zone-1, kill a unique boss / enemy in zone-1) there are player activated repeatable quests. These are great for leveling up as most of them spawn lots of enemies in an area that's just been cleared.
● TONS of other game modes for Co-op and PVP!
● In-game Map Editor is very in-depth and allows some super complex builds.
● Constant game updates. We're talking a couple a week (depending on what's added), not once every 5 months.

▼ THE BAD ▼
● Finding other players online is a bit tough since the player base is so small. This isn't really a problem with the game, just it's popularity. If you're buying Counter Spell specifically for multiplayer, make sure you have some friends to play with you.
● Online play can be very laggy depending on the host and result in game crashes.
● The Map Editor doesn't have a tutorial and is very complicated to learn.
● Ranged enemies are all over the place making the fighter classes very difficult as a starting character.
● Combat is shooting with spells / arrows or slashing with a sword. If you've played one mage, your basic attacks won't change, only your spells. There isn't any way to "fix" this, I just found the game gets a bit grindy on your second playthrough with a similar class.
● XP drops from enemies in the form of purple crystals and forces the player to collect them. This isn't so bad at first, but try doing it for the entire game. Quests give XP instantly and even playing online shares XP as soon as an enemy is killed, so I'm not sure why the crystals are there.
● Enemy AI either "sees you" or "doesn't see you yet". When activated, they'll run towards the player no matter the distance until you or they are dead. NOTE: Minions use the same AI so they will aggro everything they see. I'm not really complaining about this feature because the AI works fine for what the game is, but I didn't consider it a "good" selling feature :P

Counter Spell Official Release Game play & Review 
Counter Spell an indie action RPG which was officially released October 5, 2015
Fun old school style game!

An RPG in a FPS engine?!  Where has this game been all my life?!

Counter Spell lays the foundation for an excellent FPS-shooter engine with classic RPG elements leaving room for virtually unlimited possibilities!

PROS
+ Solid, robust FPS game engine encompassing many RPG elements (gold, experience, quests, etc)
+ RPG elements allow you to level-up and equip character with many skills and items
+ Six character classes with very different skills, spells, and play styles
+ World map is brilliantly designed with interconnecting tunnels and secret rooms and passages
+ Multitude of Co-op and PvP multiplayer modes including Capture the Flag, Deathmatch, etc.
+ Fun quest mode familiarizes you with map, character abilities, and game concepts
+ Level editor included (although I haven't used this yet)
+ Reasonable price!

CONS
- Graphics and sound, while sufficient, aren't spectacular
- First few games can be confusing (not much in terms of tutorials)
- No true AI bots in Multiplayer (random, hostile mobs are optional)
- Quest mode may have limited replayability once you learn location of hidden quest items, etc.
- The term "RPG" may be misleading as Quest Mode certainly is no FF7

For about a decade now, big budget studios have been training me to understand that the worse the graphics, the better the game, since they're not relying on grahpics and cutscenes to create the illusion of quality.

This game has proved me right yet again.  90s era graphics, great gameplay.  The artwork is still beautiful don't get me wrong, but it also has solid gameplay, lots and lots of content and multiplayer.  $7 is barely enough to buy you a kick in the arse these days, you could do worse than to spend it on a good game from an indie developer.
